evidence: Independent research corrects the premise of the retained Gao Zhan finding and blocker; it does not establish a death year. In Jinshu 108, 太興初 means early in the Taixing era, not specifically Taixing 1. The account places the Cui Bi war and Gao Zhan's transfer before Gao's death, but the death passage 瞻聞其言，彌不自安，遂以憂死 supplies no reign year. Source: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/%E6%99%89%E6%9B%B8/%E5%8D%B7108 . Local Jinshu 6 s0208–s0209 places the Cui Bi episode after the twelfth-month heading in Taixing 2; the Western designation AD 319 for Taixing 2 does not by itself convert that lunar month to an exact Western date. Zizhi Tongjian 91 groups the death account after the same twelfth-month heading and before its Taixing 3 heading, but also groups a Goguryeo attack there which Jinshu 108 explicitly places 明年, the following year. Narrative section placement alone is therefore not a reliable death-year upper bound: https://zh.wikisource.org/wiki/%E8%B3%87%E6%B2%BB%E9%80%9A%E9%91%91/%E5%8D%B7091 . In particular, the prior retained repair's onOrBefore AD 319 for Gao Zhan is not supported by these sources. A one-sided lower bound may be considered only if its Western conversion and schema requirements are independently supported; do not treat AD 319 or AD 320 as an exact death or upper bound, invent a birth year, or erase uncertainty.
